record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: (V. Kaloshin) A q0-rationally integrable billiard is elliptic. The next conjecture is motivated by a theorem of N. Innami's: if the re is a sequence of convex caustics with rotation numbers tending to 1 /2, then the billiard table is an ellipse [120] (see [3] for a simpler proof). An invariant circle of the billiard map is called rotational if it consists of periodic points.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.8. (V. Kaloshin) A q0-rationally integrable billiard is elliptic. The next conjecture is motivated by a theorem of N. Innami's: if the re is a sequence of convex caustics with rotation numbers tending to 1 /2, then the billiard table is an ellipse [120] (see [3] for a simpler proof). An invariant circle of the billiard map is called rotational if it consists of periodic points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex bounded domain, and consider the associated billiard map $T$ on the cylinder of unit inward tangent vectors at boundary points (equivalently, on pairs (boundary point, chord direction)). A smooth convex curve $\Gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a caustic of the billiard in $\Omega$ if any trajectory that is tangent to $\Gamma$ remains tangent to $\Gamma$ after each reflection from $\partial \Omega$. An invariant curve of $T$ is called rotational if it is homotopically non-trivial in the phase cylinder; such an invariant curve has a well-defined rotation number $\rho \in (0,1/2]$. For an integer $q_0 \geq 2$, say that the billiard in $\Omega$ is $q_0$-rationally integrable if, for every rational number $p/q \in (0, 1/q_0]$ with $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the billiard map admits a rotational invariant curve of rotation number $p/q$ consisting entirely of periodic points (equivalently, the billiard admits a rational caustic of rotation number $p/q$ for every such $p/q$).

Prove or disprove: every $q_0$-rationally integrable smooth strictly convex billiard table $\Omega$ is an ellipse.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (a strong form of the Birkhoff conjecture due to Kaloshin) remains open in general. Partial results are known: Kaloshin–Sorrentino and Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin proved local versions, showing that rationally integrable billiards sufficiently close to an ellipse (resp. a circle) must be ellipses. The global conjecture for $q_0$-rationally integrable billiards has not been established.

status_evidence.title: On the Local Birkhoff Conjecture for Convex Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: A small rationally integrable perturbation of an ellipse must be an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Only local (perturbative) versions of the conjecture have been proven.

status_evidence.title: Nearly circular domains which are integrable close to the boundary are ellipses
status_evidence.snippet: Rationally integrable domains close to a circle are ellipses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial/local results exist; the global Kaloshin conjecture is open.

status_evidence.title: On the integrability of Birkhoff billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing open problems including the rational integrability conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed among open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems.
